title: The Glory of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The glory of God is the display of His worth, beauty, holiness, greatness, and majesty. God’s glory is the highest purpose of creation, redemption, worship, and the life of His people.
summary: The glory of God is the display of His worth, beauty, holiness, greatness, and majesty. God’s glory is the highest purpose of creation, redemption, worship, and the life of His people.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the radiance of God’s glory and the fullest revelation of His greatness. Through Christ, God displays His glory in grace, truth, judgment, salvation, and eternal worship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s glory is not given to Him by creation as though He lacks beauty or worth. He is glorious in Himself. Creation, worship, redemption, and judgment display what is already true of Him.

The heavens declare the glory of God, and all things exist from Him, through Him, and to Him. His glory is the proper end of all things because He alone is supremely worthy.

God does not share His glory with idols. This is not selfishness, but righteousness. If God allowed anything less than Himself to become ultimate, He would deny the truth of His own worth.

In Christ, God’s glory is revealed in saving grace. The cross and resurrection show holiness, love, justice, mercy, wisdom, and power in a way that leads redeemed people to worship forever.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often live for lesser glories: approval, comfort, success, image, power, ministry recognition, or personal happiness. These cannot bear the weight of ultimate purpose.

This doctrine reorders life. The glory of God gives meaning to ordinary obedience, suffering, worship, service, and hope. Believers exist for something higher than themselves.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live for God’s glory in ordinary and visible places. Refuse to make yourself, your pain, your success, or your ministry the center. Worship Christ, serve faithfully, and ask whether your choices display the worth of God.
